column1: > Where the tunnels land, and how many clouds are on the far side.
> Columns, tab separated:
>   name       what to call the row
>   endpoints  which site nodes terminate a tunnel: cp, w1, w2, a comma
>              separated list, or all
>   remotes    1 for cloud A alone, 2 for cloud A and cloud B
> Rows are ordered so the number of clouds only grows. A remote that has
> joined stays joined; what changes between rows is which site nodes
> hold tunnels, which is a chart value. Rebuilding the whole topology per
> row would cost more than it proves.
> Every row expects total reachability: each pod reaching every other pod
> and every service, both directions, whether or not the nodes involved
> terminate a tunnel. A node with no tunnel reaches a remote by transiting
> one that has one, so tunnel placement is meant to be invisible from the
> pod network. A row that fails is that claim being wrong.
